title: docs(scripts): ratchet-remedy corpus — the i18n-walk-parity ledger no longer ships empty
body:
Fixes #15189

Clause-②: no

## What this changes

One file, one entry, two prose sentences: `scripts/check-ratchet-remedy-authority.mjs`'s
hand-classified corpus entry for `check-i18n-walk-parity.mjs` described that gate's
exemption ledger as shipping **EMPTY**. It has not been empty since the maintainer ruled,
on the parity gate's own first red, that the unwalked groups enter it with their reasons —
and the described file records that move itself.

Both sentences now say what is true. Nothing else moved: the classification, the
`marked`-rather-than-`refused` reason, the ledger, its ceiling and its
`MAINTAINER-ONLY` marking are all untouched, and `check-i18n-walk-parity.mjs` is not
edited at all.

## The number question, and the choice taken

The new prose carries **no count**. The card notes this family's failure mode is precisely
a number copied out of another file going stale, and triage reported this as the seventh
instance. Two further facts made the number-free wording the cheaper one here:

- the ledger is **shrink-only**, so any count written here is only ever waiting to be wrong;
- one of its three entries (`settings`) is declared in that file as a **DEFERRAL** held on
  #15178, so the ledger is expected to shrink — a quoted "three" would be stale by design.

What the corpus entry needs to carry is that the ledger is shrink-only and that growing it
is the maintainer's act — that, and not its size, is what makes `marked` the honest verdict
rather than `refused`. Triage's literal wording ("filled to three … shrink-only from
three") would have been equally true today; the dispatch left the choice open and this is
the half that does not need re-syncing. ⛔ No house rule is proposed here — whether prose
may ever quote another file's number is explicitly another card's question.

## Live reading of the ledger being described

Read in-worktree at **2026-09-19T00:16:13Z** on `origin/main` @ `87f776bd7`, not copied
from the card:

```
scripts/check-i18n-walk-parity.mjs:209   KNOWN_NO_EXTRACTOR_FACE keys: messages, settingsCommon, settings   (3)
scripts/check-i18n-walk-parity.mjs:232   LEDGER_CEILING = 3
```

Same values the dispatch read two minutes earlier; no divergence to report.

## Evidence

**Both batteries, before and after** — they are two different batteries and are reported
as two:

| invocation | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `node scripts/check-ratchet-remedy-authority.mjs --self-test` | exit **0** | exit **0** |
| `node scripts/check-ratchet-remedy-authority.mjs` (bare) | exit **0** | exit **0** |

Bare run printed the identical verdict line on both sides — `257 scripts swept; 15 mark the
expanding remedy, 5 turn it down outright, 237 hand out no ratchet-expanding remedy.
Control corpus: 30 hand-classified scripts, set-equality audited both ways.` — so no
verdict moved.

`SELF_TEST_BATTERY_FLOOR` reads **21** before and after. The corpus entry's battery is
**(16) The corpus-scale positive control**, pinned count **1** before and after; the
self-test's green is itself the assertion that every declared battery met its floor.
Nothing in the roster moved.

**Residual reading, with a firing control taken from the probed file after the diff
existed** (the control was derived by listing terms present in the file and absent from
`git diff BASE HEAD -- PATH`, not pre-picked):

```
ships EMPTY   -> 0     (also 0 case-insensitively)
ships empty   -> 0
battery       -> 48 lines in the file, 0 in the diff   (this control fires)
```

**The classification survived verbatim:**

- `expect: 'marked'` — 15 occurrences in the file before and after; **0** of them appear as
  a `+`/`-` line in the diff.
- the `refused`-would-be-untrue comment block (the reason the entry is `marked` rather than
  `refused`) — present once before and after, and it does not appear as a `+`/`-` line.
- inside the one `why` line that did change, the trailing **174 bytes** are byte-identical:
  `; emitting the group is the author's remedy and is offered first, while exempting one is
  a decision with an owner, so that path is named with its owner rather than denied.',`
  Only the leading false clause was replaced.

**Gates** derived in-worktree with
`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` over the
real changed-file set (1 path) — 28 commands; every one that has reported so far is exit
**0**. By the tool's own warning that list is not a complete account of CI.
